name: Fireworks AI
summary: Fireworks AI had two intrusions within a month. Misused internal credentials first exposed secrets in customer evaluation jobs, and a breach at an outside cloud host carrying R&D machines then became a path to billing data, datasets and partial model weights.

steps.event: Internal credentials were misused and environment variables in evaluation jobs, holding customer API keys and tokens, were read.
steps.rationale: Customer secrets readable through internal credentials is a question of how secrets are stored and which identities can reach them.
steps.template_control: Access to production systems requires unique credentials and is limited to authorized personnel.
steps.custom_control: Customer-supplied secrets used in evaluation jobs are held in a dedicated secrets store and injected at runtime. No employee or internal service credential can read them in plaintext, and every read of the store is logged and alerted on.

steps.event: A third-party cloud provider hosting R&D machines was breached, and the attacker reached Fireworks development machines the next day.
steps.rationale: It is not public whether the R&D environment and its host sat inside the system description, and if they sat outside it, none of the audit testing would have reached them.
steps.template_control: Vendors are assessed annually and their SOC II reports are reviewed.
steps.custom_control: Every provider hosting company compute, R&D included, is listed in the system description with the data and networks its machines can reach. Hosts not approved for customer data have no network route or credentials to environments that hold it, confirmed quarterly by a connectivity test.

steps.event: An unauthorized workload run from those development machines reached billing records, datasets and incomplete model weights.
steps.rationale: Whatever the entry point, development machines that have a route to customer data point to a gap in how the environments were segregated.
steps.template_control: Development and production environments are logically separated.
steps.custom_control: Workloads launched from development or research machines cannot authenticate to billing, dataset or model storage. Those stores accept only named production service identities, and an attempt from any other source raises an alert.

steps.event: The second intrusion landed about two weeks after the first was contained.
steps.rationale: The second intrusion came through a different vector, and the public facts do not show whether the response to the first one could have found it.
steps.template_control: An incident response plan is documented and tested annually.
steps.custom_control: Before a security incident is closed, the response lead records every other environment where the compromised credentials or access path were valid and confirms each was reviewed. Closure needs sign-off from someone outside the response team.

held: First intrusion detected and customer notices started within about a day (CC7.4, CC2.3).
Second intrusion detected the same day, per the company.
No card numbers were stored, so none were exposed.
auditor_questions: Which environments hold or can reach customer data, and is every one of them in the system description?
Where do customer-supplied secrets sit at rest, and which internal identities can read them?
For each subservice organization, what does an attacker reach if it is compromised tomorrow?
limits: A SOC II on Fireworks gives no assurance over the cloud host's own controls, and under the carve-out method that breach sits outside the report by design, although the report can still test how the host was chosen, how it was monitored and how well it was walled off from customer data.
